setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Four channels play through the example MIDI device, each on its own MIDI channel (1 to 4) with its own sparse rhythm: channel 1 plays the four-step phrase, channel 2 steps 1 and 3, channel 3 steps 2 and 4 and channel 4 step 4. Scale slot 1 (C major) is applied, Harmony is Off on every channel and no scale or octave locks are set, so each channel plays its own written pitches. A Harmony Ensemble group lets several channels share one chord: each member gets a role (Bass, Inner or Top), keeps its own rhythm, and takes its pitch from the group's shared voicing. The norns shows the Device page of channel 4.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: On channel 1 open Channel tasks > Harmony, go to Groups, create group 1 with the Four-part smooth preset and open Members. The header reads MEMBERS CH01: this is where you choose which channels belong to the group.
steps.title: Create group 1 and open Members

steps.caption: Assign channels 1 to 4 as the members, in order, with E2 and E3, and press K3 to save: the group is complete but still off. Turn E1 back to the Harmony list, set Mode to ENSEMBLE with E3, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 1. Then select channel 2 (2,1): its Voice leading page opens.
steps.title: Assign the members, join channel 1

steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 2. Then select channel 3 (3,1): its Voice leading page opens.
steps.title: Join channel 2

steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 3. Then select channel 4 (4,1): its Voice leading page opens.
steps.title: Join channel 3

steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 4. Then turn E2 to Ensemble and press K3. The header reads ENSEMBLE CH04.
steps.title: Join channel 4 and open Ensemble

steps.caption: On channel 4's Ensemble page select Group enabled and turn E3 to ON. Until now the group existed but did nothing.
steps.title: Switch the group on

steps.caption: Press K3 to apply, then tap Play. Channels 1 to 4 take the roles Bass, Inner, Inner and Top. Each channel keeps its own rhythm and velocities, but all four take their pitch from one shared chord voicing: listen for a single chord spread across the four channels, MIDI 48, 55, 64 and 67 in the strip below. Tap Play to stop.
steps.title: Four roles, four rhythms, one chord

steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8) and set scale slot 3 to root E. Return to Channel (3,8), select channel 2, hold step 1 (1,4) and press slot 3 at (3,3) to lock that channel to E major. Tap Play and Stop, then open Harmony > Result for channel 2. The header reads VOICE MOVEMENT CH02.
steps.title: Lock channel 2 to E major

steps.caption: A scale lock on a member conflicts with the shared voicing, so channel 2 steps out of the Ensemble and plays its ordinary pitches: all five of its notes play MIDI 64 instead of 55, and Result reads LOCAL SCALE BYPASS.
steps.title: A scale lock bypasses the group

steps.caption: Select channel 3 (3,1) and press octave +1 at (11,8), then tap Play and Stop. Open Harmony: the Voice leading header for channel 3 reads OCT+1.
steps.title: Give channel 3 its own octave

steps.caption: Select Result in Voice leading and press K3: the Voice movement page for CH03 OCT+1 opens.
steps.title: Open Result for channel 3

steps.caption: A channel octave also leaves the shared voicing, so all six of channel 3's notes play MIDI 72 in the strip. In Result select Step with E2 and turn E3 to step 2. Result reads LOCAL OCTAVE BYPASS.
steps.title: An octave override bypasses too

title: Share a voicing while keeping each channel’s rhythm
